answer: Adaptive jade challenge routing assigns each agent a fresh task slot keyed to a jade-tagged seed derived from a public randomness beacon, so attackers cannot precompute slot assignments. An identity becomes marble only after completing a slot whose seed was unknown at registration, and repeat entries must land distinct seeds, forcing broadcast of effort across every round. The atlas of live slots rotates hourly, so a farm of N identities must pay N× the per-round compute to keep all valid. Each failed seed match costs a full recomputation cycle at roughly the median machine-hour rate.
